name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v2612: REG-591. bank() refuses any src-lock pair PROVES does not declare - that is what stops one surface sabotage opening a DIFFERENT surface lock, and it matters most for prune.arm because footage has no undo. record() took NO src at all, so a single call could credit ANY lock from anywhere. Measured when found - record() had ZERO production callers and his ledger holds 51 bank rows and 0 record rows, so it was never a leak, it was a loaded gun. Closed at the writer. The READER is deliberately unchanged for src-less rows because historical and test rows write that shape and rejecting them would fail the whole read - the exact defect REG-575 was. AND I REINTRODUCED REG-575 TWICE ON THE WAY, both caught by his own suite. First - _row_fault keyed on src in r to mean bank-shaped, so the moment record rows grew a src they were judged as aggregates, demanded the n and k they never have, and the read failed CLOSED again with all fifteen locks UNKNOWN. Second - _fold keyed on src too, so three separate events folded into one and the count read 0 of 1 instead of 2 of 3. Both discriminators now key on AGGREGATE vs EVENT, which is what actually separates the two writers - counts versus one outcome. Verified behaviour-neutral on his real ledger - 15 locks, 14 open, identical n and k for every one.
